chunks: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said to me:
'By Allah! We are indeed the treasurers of Allah in His sky and His earth — not over gold, and not over silver, but over His Knowledge.'

key_terms.خُزَّانُ: Treasurers/custodians — those entrusted with safeguarding a treasury; here denotes the Imams as guardians of divine knowledge
key_terms.سَمَاء: Sky/heaven — the celestial realm, paired with earth to indicate the universality of their custodianship
key_terms.عِلْمِهِ: His (God's) knowledge — the divine knowledge transmitted to the Imams exclusively

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Baqir say about the Imams being treasurers of Allah's knowledge?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) declares to his companion Sawrat ibn Kulayb that the Imams of Ahl al-Bayt are the custodians of divine knowledge — not worldly treasures like gold or silver, but the sacred knowledge bestowed upon them by Allah. This hadith establishes the theological basis of the Imams' exclusive custodianship of divine knowledge, a cornerstone of Shia doctrine on the Imamate. The statement was made in a private setting, emphasizing the intimate transmission of this creedal teaching from Imam to companion.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Husayn Bin Saeed, from Ali Bin Asbaat, from his father Asbaat, from Sowrat Bin Kuleyb who said,

‘Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> said to me: ‘By Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! We<sup>asws</sup> are the treasurers of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> in His<sup>azwj</sup> sky and His<sup>azwj</sup> earth, neither upon gold nor upon silver, but upon His<sup>azwj</sup> Knowledge’.
en.sarwar: 2. A number of our people has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from Ali ibn Asbat from his father, Asbat from Sawra ibn Kulayb who has said that Imam abu Ja’far (a.s.) said to him the following. “
I swear to Allah that we are the treasurers of Allah in His heavens and on His earth but the treasurers of gold or the treasurers of silver but the treasurers of His knowledge.”.
